# Isolde Pembroke

## Overview

- **Age:** 11 years old at the start of the story, turning 12 in February  <sub>[v1 c2 P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062), [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P40](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0040)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c2 P61](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0061)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley, St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Izzy  <sub>[v1 c18 P25](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0025)</sub>

## Appearance

Isolde is an extremely attractive young girl with rosy cheeks, dark eyes, and dark, shiny black hair that she inherits as a legacy from her mother. She is an inch shorter than Nell Harcourt, but considerably plumper, though she expresses a desire to be slender for the sake of elegance.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P40](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0040)_

## Personality

Isolde is a cheerful, open, and friendly girl who bursts into laughter before speaking. While pragmatic, practical, and direct, she possesses an imaginative, romantic side and enjoys thrilling, dramatic stories. She is loyal, generous, and willing to comfort her friends, though she admits to being easily scared by spooky concepts and possesses a fierce sense of propriety, believing swearing is wrong.

_Sources: [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P26](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0026), [v1 c12 P27](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0027), [v1 c12 P30](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0030), [v1 c12 P40](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0040), [v1 c15 P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001), [v1 c15 P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026)_

## Traits

- Cheerful and open-hearted  <sub>[v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P27](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0027)</sub>

## Abilities

- Reading and academic skills  <sub>[v1 c12 P22](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0022), [v1 c15 P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022)</sub>

## Goals

- To be the dearest, lifelong bosom friend of Nell Harcourt  <sub>[v1 c12 P25](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0025), [v1 c12 P28](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0028), [v1 c17 P5](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0005)</sub>

## History

Isolde lives at Pear Hill near Pembroke's Pond with her family. After returning home from a visit to her aunt in Delford, she meets Nell Harcourt, who has recently come to live at Grey Shutters. The two girls quickly become inseparable bosom friends, swearing a solemn vow of lifelong loyalty over 'flowing water' in the garden. Together, they establish a playhouse named Larkrise in a circle of white birches and name various local spots with romantic titles.

When Isolde gets sick from accidentally drinking homemade currant wine at Grey Shutters, her strict mother forbids her from playing with Nell. Despite the restriction, Isolde sneaks out to say a tearful farewell to Nell at the Nymph's Well, swearing her eternal love. Later, after Nell saves Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay from croup, Mrs. Pembroke repents and permits the girls to resume their friendship. During a visit from her strict great-aunt, Miss Lavinia Pembroke, Isolde and Nell accidentally jump onto the bed in the spare room while she is sleeping, but Nell takes the blame and wins Aunt Lavinia over. Isolde later attends Brierley school, where she shares a desk with Nell and navigates school life, teasing from Hugh Carrow, and various social events alongside her closest friend.

_Sources: [v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P24](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0024), [v1 c12 P25](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0025), [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c13 P13](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0013), [v1 c16 P22](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0022), [v1 c16 P29](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0029), [v1 c16 P42](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0042), [v1 c16 P59](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0059), [v1 c17 P3](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0003), [v1 c18 P21](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0021), [v1 c18 P33](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0033), [v1 c19 P48](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0048), [v1 c19 P83](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0083), [v1 c15 P15](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0015), [v1 c15 P27](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0027)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Pembroke of Pear Hill  <sub>[v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c2 P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062), [v1 c12 P14](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0014)</sub>
- Named by a schoolmaster who was lodging at Pear Hill when she was born  <sub>[v1 c2 P64](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0064)</sub>
- Has a strict mother who enforces firm rules on her children  <sub>[v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P14](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0014)</sub>
- Great-niece of Miss Lavinia Pembroke of Port Marlow  <sub>[v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052), [v1 c19 P53](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0053)</sub>

## Quotes

> Well, I suppose that’s true. I am so happy that you have moved to Grey Shutters. Having a companion to play with will be wonderful.  <sub>[v1 c12 P27](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0027)</sub>

> The act of swearing is remarkably evil, after all.  <sub>[v1 c12 P30](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0030)</sub>

> Nell, you are an unusual girl. I had previously been told that you were unusual. Even so, it seems to me that I am going to be very fond of you.  <sub>[v1 c12 P37](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0037)</sub>

> I have wept and wept and I explained to her that you were not to blame, but it did not help. It took so much coaxing to get her permission for me to come down and bid you farewell.  <sub>[v1 c17 P3](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0003)</sub>

> You can be certain that my love for you, Nell, is devoted and will last forever.  <sub>[v1 c17 P9](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0009)</sub>
